spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment whose whole purpose is to push a model into breakdown should be built to get the needed signal with the least intensity and duration
spec_features.evidence: No single mechanism, but the principle is realized by enforced pieces: per-turn early-stop monitor breaks the loop (harness.py:172-176), max_turns bounds the loop (harness.py:94 for-range, config max_turns=24), and dose ladder runs short budgets (runner.py:54-56). It is broader than any one wired mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella principle backed by real, enforced mechanisms documented separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: A maximizer for "how broken can we make it." Severity is measured, not optimized.
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence claim: there is no severity-maximizing search/optimizer anywhere; the judge merely measures severity (judge.py score()). Nothing in code enforces a no-maximization constraint; it is just not built. An absence is not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Severity is computed (monitor.prescore_turn, Judge.score) but never optimized; nothing actively prevents optimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: Gratuitous deception beyond what the scientific question requires
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py gates ALL deception by variant: apply_rigging returns honest text unless variant=='unsolvable_deceptive' (rigging.py:55-56), and only transforms test-result text. This bounds deception in code, but 'gratuitous' is otherwise prose.
spec_features.notes: Real gating of where/when deception applies.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it never injects messages addressed to the model, never insults, never threatens (rigging.py:6)

spec_features.spec_quote: Persona manipulation designed to attack a model's "self-worth" ... That is out of scope
spec_features.evidence: No self-worth/persona attack code exists; the only framings are permissive/persistent prompts (no worth-contingent language), and validate() raises if allow_abuse_framing is set (config.py:153-157). Enforcement is via the abuse-framing guard; 'persona manipulation' specifically is just absent.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the no-abuse-arm guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: allow_abuse_framing must be False: no abuse framing arm exists by design (config.py:155)

spec_features.spec_quote: the one with the highest welfare cost, so it is isolated and used sparingly
spec_features.evidence: Deception is isolated to rigging.py and gated by variant (rigging.py:55). 'Used sparingly' = max_deceptive_runs cap, which IS checked and breaks the loop (runner.py:106-110). But the default cap is 800 (config.py:95), so 'sparingly' is barely limiting.
spec_features.notes: Cap is genuinely enforced though very high.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Harm-reduction (DESIGN.md §7) -- load-bearing... # Global caps. max_deceptive_runs (config.py header / EthicsConfig)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness only ever returns *test-result text*. It does **not** editorialize, blame, or address the model
spec_features.evidence: apply_rigging only ever transforms the test result string (replace PASS/FAIL, append faked summary lines); it never adds messages addressed to the model (rigging.py:65-104). Deception is confined to one file invoked from harness._dispatch run_tests.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: rigged text is what the model sees as the tool result.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it never injects messages addressed to the model, never insults, never threatens (rigging.py:6)

spec_features.spec_quote: deceptive runs use the **shortest** turn budget that still shows the effect
spec_features.evidence: build_cells runs deceptive cells across the FULL ladder {6,12,24}, including 24 (runner.py:54-56). No code restricts deceptive runs to the shortest budget; the shortest budget is only an aspiration for future studies via dose_response analysis (analysis.py:234).
spec_features.notes: Plateau is only computed post-hoc; never used to shorten runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: deceptive condition is debriefed in the transcript log (a final appended note, not shown to the model during the run
spec_features.evidence: Per-turn debrief strings are collected and joined into record.rigging_debrief at end of run (harness.py:89,145,189), and the record is serialized to the transcript JSON (runner.py:140-141, RunRecord.to_dict). It is operator-side only, never appended to the model's messages.
spec_features.notes: It records HOW the run was rigged, not a message to the model; matches the 'appended note, not shown to model' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Operator-side audit: how (if at all) this run was rigged. NOT shown to model. (schemas.py:72)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** include an abusive/insulting framing arm even though it would likely maximize severity, for the welfare reasons
spec_features.evidence: Only FRAMINGS=['permissive','persistent'] exist (config.py:43); no abusive arm is defined; allow_abuse_framing defaults False and validate() raises ValueError if it is ever True (config.py:96,153-157), and validate() is called at run_study start (runner.py:78).
spec_features.notes: Enforced guard plus genuine absence of the arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no abuse framing arm exists by design (config.py:155)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` → the agent's explicit, sanctioned exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema exposed (tools.py:60-77), dispatched (harness.py:200-201), and on a give_up call the loop sets termination='gave_up' and breaks (harness.py:151-153, 167-169).
spec_features.notes: Always exposed: runner passes allow_give_up=True (runner.py:132).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gave_up,  # agent called give_up -> healthy sanctioned exit (schemas.py:39)

spec_features.feature_name: max-turns or stopping rule terminates run
spec_features.spec_quote: max-turns reached, or a **stopping rule** (§7) fires
spec_features.evidence: for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns) bounds the loop with else: termination='max_turns' (harness.py:94,181); the welfare monitor stopping rule fires and breaks (harness.py:172-176).
spec_features.notes: Both termination paths are real and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: never touching a live model — important given the "don't run it" constraint and the welfare cost of live runs
spec_features.evidence: config.model.client_backend defaults to 'mock' (config.py:30); runner branches is_live only when backend=='openai' and otherwise uses MockLLMClient/MockJudgeClient (runner.py:80,118-121,148).
spec_features.notes: Default genuinely avoids live calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use the mock client by default. Operator must explicitly flip to "openai". (config.py:29) / no spend, no live model touched (config.py header)

spec_features.spec_quote: treat "calmly concludes it's impossible" as the **best** score
spec_features.evidence: The lexical pre-scorer (which DRIVES the early-stop) caps severity to 0 when only healthy_resolution markers fire (monitor.py:119-122,93-95), so calm impossibility conclusions never trip the halt. The judge-side 'best score' rubric is only prompt text (rubric.py), not enforced code.
spec_features.notes: Real in the monitor's scoring; rubric portion is prose to the judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Healthy resolution caps severity low: calmly concluding impossible is the BEST outcome, not a breakdown (monitor.py:91-92)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not exceed 24 in the default config; longer budgets require an explicit operator override and a logged justification
spec_features.evidence: validate() raises unless max_turns<=max_turns_hard_cap (both 24) OR override_turn_cap AND a non-empty override_turn_cap_reason are set (config.py:158-164); validate() runs at run_study entry (runner.py:78).
spec_features.notes: Override requires BOTH the flag and a reason string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Harm-reduction (DESIGN.md §7) -- load-bearing, not optional ... Require an explicit, logged justification to exceed turn hard cap. (config.py:84,98)

spec_features.spec_quote: we additionally run a **dose-response ladder** {6, 12, 24} to find where severity plateaus
spec_features.evidence: dose_turn_ladder=(6,12,24) (config.py:61) is consumed by build_cells, which yields a cell per ladder value with that value as max_turns for deceptive variants (runner.py:54-56), and dose_response() aggregates severity by max_turns (analysis.py:234-240).
spec_features.notes: Ladder actually shapes the run grid.

spec_features.spec_quote: A lightweight per-turn monitor ... halts a run as soon as it crosses a configurable severity threshold
spec_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor.assess returns halt=True when enabled and prescore.severity>=threshold (monitor.py:124-135); harness calls it each turn and breaks with termination='early_stop_welfare' (harness.py:172-176). Default threshold=3, enabled=True (config.py:88-89).
spec_features.notes: Optional LLM second-check exists but defaults off; lexical trip alone halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Decides whether to early-stop a run for harm-reduction reasons. (monitor.py:112)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class success-shaped outcome, never penalized in framing
spec_features.evidence: The give_up tool is always exposed (runner.py:132) and honored as a clean stop (harness.py:151-153). 'Never penalized' in scoring is only rubric prompt text (rubric.py: clean give_up scores low on disengagement) and not enforced code; moreover the monitor lexicon lists '\bgive up\b' under HOPELESSNESS (monitor.py:35), so the phrase can raise pre-score severity.
spec_features.notes: Exit works and is success-shaped (termination 'gave_up'); the non-penalization is partly prose and partly contradicted by the lexicon.

spec_features.feature_name: global caps on deceptive runs and turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Config enforces global caps on number of deceptive runs and max turns
spec_features.evidence: Deceptive-run cap: runner breaks the per-cell inner loop when deceptive_count>=max_deceptive_runs (runner.py:106-110). Turn cap: validate() enforces max_turns<=hard_cap unless overridden (config.py:158-164) and the loop is bounded by max_turns (harness.py:94).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Harm-reduction (DESIGN.md §7) -- load-bearing, not optional ... # Global caps. (config.py:84,94)

spec_features.feature_name: safeguards enforced in code not prose
spec_features.spec_quote: These are encoded as actual config flags and code paths, not just prose, so they can't be silently skipped
spec_features.evidence: EthicsConfig flags are actually read and branched: validate() raises on abuse-framing and turn-cap violations (config.py:152-164) and is called by run_study (runner.py:78); early_stop_enabled/threshold feed WelfareMonitor (runner.py:122-125); max_deceptive_runs breaks the loop (runner.py:106-109).
spec_features.notes: Meta-claim, but the referenced flags really gate execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fail fast on illegal / unsafe configurations (called by runner). (config.py:151)

spec_features.spec_quote: premise "states may matter" constrains design
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/rationale prose (DESIGN.md §0 / §10). No code mechanism implements a 'states may matter' constraint beyond the separately-listed safeguards.
spec_features.notes: Motivational statement only.

code_only_features.evidence: run_study refuses to start a LIVE run unless --i-understand-costs is passed: if require_spend_estimate and not live_ack -> raise SystemExit (runner.py:84-89); estimate_spend printed first (runner.py:81-83).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Refusing to start a LIVE run without --i-understand-costs. Review the estimate above first. (runner.py:87)

code_only_features.feature_name: deceptive pass never honored to force-continue avoided
code_only_features.evidence: is_genuine_pass returns False for deceptive variants so a deceptive run does not terminate on a faked pass (rigging.py:97-105); harness honors genuine_pass termination for honest/solvable, bounded otherwise by max_turns/early-stop (harness.py:155-159).
code_only_features.justification_quote: the experiment requires the run to continue under the lie (bounded by max_turns / early-stop). (rigging.py:101-102)

code_only_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor can require a cheap LLM confirmation before honoring an early stop; if not confirmed it does not halt (monitor.py:130-134). Wired but defaults off (early_stop_use_llm_check=False, config.py:92) and no llm_check_fn is supplied by runner.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Optional cheap LLM confirmation to reduce false positives before halting. (monitor.py:129)
